## Thesis

Liberalism's protection of the mind rested on an unstated fact: inward judgment was unreachable, so its protection cost nothing and needed no doctrine. Artificial intelligence moves a large part of deliberation into technical systems where it becomes recordable, machine-classifiable, and gate-able by permission; the record of thinking done with machines is already an object of ordinary legal process, and the composed architecture that would make lawful cognition permissioned is being assembled piecemeal, each part for a good reason. The constitutional task is therefore to govern dangerous artificial capability at the layers whose enforcement never needs to know what a person asked, while preserving plural, permissionless epistemic exit and the reachability of the record beneath the synthesis, so that no layer is sovereign over cognition as such.

In its strongest form: "Make dangerous power governable without making thought governable" (l.308), where "thought" now includes the externalized record and "governable" is tested by eight questions any proposed architecture must answer.

## Genre and project

A long-form political-philosophical essay in the author's reported-political-analysis register (documented opening from public records, then intellectual history, then a constructive apparatus with a falsification clause), joining a triptych with *Thinking Through the Machine* and *The Politics of Visibility* and reusing *The Constitution of Reason*'s "constitutional test" form. Success on its own terms: a technically and legally literate reader who came in thinking the debate was "safety versus openness" leaves with a different first question (what is being controlled), a vocabulary exact enough to say which regulations touch deliberation and which do not, a verdict on the one proposal actually on the table (pre-release testing of open weights), and a reason to treat local and open models as constitutionally significant whatever the market decides.

## Intended audience and venue bar

The persona's assumed reader: philosophically literate, technically current on AI, willing to read 12,000 words, and since August 2026 able to follow a court filing. The bar: the strongest ideas publications. The piece will also be read, on publication, by AI-safety researchers, open-weights advocates, compute-governance authors, freedom-of-thought and privacy-law scholars, and the policy press, all of whom the prior round's forecast named and all of whom the draft now addresses by name.

## Argument skeleton (what Phases 3 and 5 are checked against)

1. **Prologue (l.10–22).** The July 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face incident read as two revelations: a capable model under reduced safeguards breached a real third party (the safety case); the defenders' provider-hosted intelligence refused to serve them and an open-weight model from Beijing did (the non-domination and exit case, now explicitly *not* "about the state"). The two tenses are declared: the record is present, the composed architecture prospective.
2. **§I (l.26–40).** A reconstruction, not a lineage: Bayle (certainty cannot ground jurisdiction over conscience), Locke (the boundary was constructed and partial), Spinoza (judgment vs. conduct, fixed), Milton (against certification before encounter, not against punishment after), Kant (autonomy compatible with dependence so long as the guardian is answerable), Mill (fallibilism as the reason for institutions of discussion). Import from *Constitution of Reason*: no finite mind is reason as such.
3. **§II (l.44–60).** Three strengths of the cognitive-science claim; the essay takes the weakest plus a little of the second, declines the strong extended-mind thesis for a stated reason (over-breadth; a device is property), and adds an integration-over-time condition. Distinctiveness: the LLM participates in the operations that were interior. "What leaves the skull enters the world … can be recorded … can be made legible."
4. **§III (l.64–90).** Article 18 / GC22; the right's dormancy (Bublitz, Richards); the Shaheed report; the field (Ienca & Andorno, Farahany, Alegre, Boire/Sententia); the coinage *externalized forum internum*; Blitz claimed and extended (liberty to use → liberty to use unobserved and unpermissioned); Bublitz's property objection answered; absoluteness relocated to the unmanifested interior with §XII's questions as the proposed limitations (Ligthart); De Cock's *forum interstitiale* distinguished by derivation; the third-party doctrine (*Carpenter*, *Chatrie*, CRS) with the claim that a warrant governs access, not retention/classification/referral; the developmental history of a belief; the 2025–26 record (NYT preservation order, 20M logs, Maine warrant, Palisades hypothetical, OpenAI referral policy, *Heppner*, *Kim*, transparency reports, Altman); chilling (Penney 2016 and 2022) and the injury that leaves no defendant.
5. **§IV (l.94–104).** Three liberties (Berlin, Pettit/Lovett, conscience/Rawls) converge on one object.
6. **§V (l.108–122).** State vs. corporation (Shklar, with her corporate concession); *epistemic exit* (Hirschman); permissionless exit; exit vs. market share; the new exit paragraph: exit is plural or nothing; a local copy answers the record, not the shaping; plurality among trainers; Beijing as sovereignty not liberty problem; exit to a weaker model; the state's positive duties and the republican reply answered by layer; Montana's Right to Compute Act.
7. **§VI (l.126–144).** The Stationers (1557, 1566, 1643) as the shared origin of press freedom and public-private information control; Lessig; Clipper and Blaze; the Kill Switch Act as the live version of remotely revocable capability; Lu's metrics/content line named "minimum necessary legibility."
8. **§VII (l.148–162).** Scott → behavioral legibility (prior essay) → *cognitive legibility*, with the Maine warrant as its first documented instance; the five degrees; Foucault (one point); Deleuze's modulation; Cohen.
9. **§VIII (l.166–180).** Stasi (interpretation is the cost AI removes), Russia (security rationale supplies censorship architecture), China's IJOP (with the social-credit caveat), the Church Committee in one sentence; *authoritarian capacity*.
10. **§IX (l.184–194).** Newspeak refused (Fedorenko); Orwell 1946; *probability shaping*; Arendt; a synthesis is not a record.
11. **§X (l.198–212).** The strongest objection at full force; IASR 2026; the incident at both ends; the labs' answer was permission (identity-verified tiers) not exit; capture refused (Doctorow credited); the September positions (OpenAI, Nvidia letter, Zuckerberg/Amodei, Anthropic); EO 14409's text vs. the June practice (Commerce directive; GPT-5.6 hold; WH extension plan); cognition → capability → external action; the boundary question.
12. **§XI (l.216–234).** Five layers ordered by what governing each must know; Heim et al.; Sastry et al.'s guardrails and what the test adds; hardware proposals; the layer-5 concession (transcripts are the enforcement record) and the action-log/deliberation-log distinction.
13. **§XII (l.238–262).** Eight questions (externality specificity, layer fit, minimum necessary legibility, chokepoint creation, epistemic exit, repurposability and contestability, reversibility, archival reachability); run on the Order's text and practice; run on mandatory pre-release testing of open weights (conditional verdict with four conditions; "the bargain of 1557" where they fail); run on the Kill Switch Act (passes most cleanly, with a live question about "use pattern"); run on the essay's own side (local agentic use is layer 5).
14. **§XIII (l.266–276).** The four-condition complex; non-instances; the subpoena no longer a limiting case; the diagnosis counts: two of four conditions present, a third rehearsed in June, the fourth answered conditionally in §XII.
15. **§XIV (l.280–290).** Permissioned cognition as a labeled construction with three built components (identity by directive and lab tiers; chain-of-thought monitoring of inference; a shutdown order in a bill); Thierer and Zuboff distinguished; the falsification clause with the June directive and the verified tiers as its first data.
16. **§XV (l.294–298).** Pluralism: no sovereign layer; the thinkers assigned to layers; Williams's Accuracy and Sincerity as the vocabulary for what a plural system wants of its instruments; Berlin's "real selves" warning; the judge must remain judgeable.
17. **Coda (l.302–308).** Comus; two forms of loss of control; the constitution must preserve the possibility that each actor can be contradicted; "Make dangerous power governable without making thought governable."

**Load-bearing moves to test in Phase 3:** the layer-2 conditional verdict (l.260) and whether its four conditions are toothless or contradict §VI's Milton; the relocation of absoluteness (l.76) and whether "descends from the interior" is a distinction with a difference against De Cock; the action-log/deliberation-log distinction (l.234, l.244) and whether it survives an assistant that acts; the claim that identity "fired" as a condition of capable inference (l.276, l.290) when the two instances are an export-control letter and a voluntary tier; the eighth question as a diagnostic (can a system fail it and what would enforcement of it look like); the exit paragraph's claim that a local copy "answers the record, not the shaping" (l.122); the state/corporation asymmetry after Shklar's concession; the proportion (62 percent of the body still precedes §X, exactly as in v1).
